Because infected ticks were able to transmit both Ip36-minus and Ip36* B. burgdorferito a limited number of mice, we were now in a position to ask whether or not uninfected larvae could acquire these spirochetes naturally by feeding on infected mice, in order to complete the infectious cycle. Approximately 100 uninfected

I. scapularis larvae were fed to repletion on mice infected with either B. burgdorferi clone A3-M9 Ip36-minus or

A3-M9 Ip36-minus/Ip36-gent. Larvae were assessed for the presence and density of spirochetes in the midguts 7 days post feeding by IFA and plating of dilutions of triturated whole ticks. No spirochetes were detected by either IFA or plating of nine larvae that fed on mice infected with spirochetes lacking Ip36, while eight out of nine of the larvae that fed on mice infected with Ip36'

B. burgdorfer harboured live spirochetes.

There was no statistical difference in the absolute number of mice that became infected by tick bite with Ip36-minus compared with Ip36 B. burgdorferi (Table 3).

Because there was evidence that the number of infected tissues was reduced in mice infected with spirochetes lacking Ip36 compared with mice infected with Ip36* spirochetes, the data were also compared using an exact permutation test, which took into account the average number of infected tissues per mouse. The P-values for the difference between the number of infected tissues per mouse infected with Ip36-minus or Ip36-minus/lp36-gent spirochetes by larval or nymphal tick bite were 0.05 and 0.02 respectively. Although there was little to no Ip36- dependent statistical difference in mouse infection by tick bite, there was a trend towards a difference that was not detectable given the small sample size. Moreover, there was a biological difference between the mice infected by tick bite with Ip36-minus compared to Ip36' spirochetes.

The serological response to Borrelia proteins of mice infected with Ip36-minus spirochetes was reduced relative to mice infected with Ip36 spirochetes (Fig. 1B), Ip36- minus spirochetes were reisolated from limited tissues (Table 3), and were only detected in the ear tissue by qPCR (Fig. 3A). Finally, although a proportion of the mice fed on by ticks infected with Ip36-minus spirochetes became infected, uninfected larvae did not acquire Ip36-minus spirochetes by feeding on these mice, demonstrating that this infection does not permit efficient maintenance of B. burgdorferi in the infectious cycle.

Borrelia burgdorferi lacking Jp36 are highly attenuated relative to isogenic Ip36 spirochetes
